I have farmed for many years, so I will stay with a steady, practical approach instead of taking risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and manage weeds and disease with limited pesticide sprays so I can protect yield without overspending. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 6.0 mu with hybrid seed, because maize responds well and gives me stable production in this system. Since some family labor is off-farm and the household is small, I will choose rotary tillage and input levels that I know I can manage in time. My goal is stable yield and controllable cost, not chasing the highest possible output.
